note: Continental silver marks (town, inspection, standard, duty marks and date letters) as Okie printed them in Old Silver and Old Sheffield Plate (1928). Built by hallmark-sources/pagekit/export_okie.py.

okie-1928.author: Howard Pitcher Okie
okie-1928.title: Old Silver and Old Sheffield Plate

eu20-austria-hungary-czpunc-old.title: Puncovní úřad (Czech Assay Office), "Staré puncovní značky uznávané jako platné" (2025, V1), 12 pp. with drawings of all Austrian, Czechoslovak, Protectorate and Slovak marks
eu20-austria-hungary-czpunc-old.gloss: Old hallmarks recognised as valid. The Czech state assay office lists the marks of the lot system, the 1824 law, the 1866 law (RGBl. 75/1866), the 1921, 1929 and 1941 Czechoslovak/Protectorate/Slovak marks, with fineness values, laws and dates.

eu20-austria-hungary-neuwirth-1980.title: Waltraud Neuwirth, Wiener Jugendstilsilber - Original, Faelschung oder Pasticcio? (Wien 1980), pp. 85-88, reproduced at wienersilber.at "Punzierung 1867-1922"
eu20-austria-hungary-neuwirth-1980.gloss: Reproduces the Austrian Finance Ministry decree of 30 Nov 1866 (Beilage A office list, Beilage B drawings of the stamps) and the decree of 19 March 1872 (office letters merged into the fineness stamps), with the meaning of the numerals 1-4.

eu20-austria-hungary-okie-1928.title: Howard Pitcher Okie, Old Silver and Old Sheffield Plate (New York, 1928), "Marks on Other Continental Plate", Austria and Hungary, printed pp. 355-359 (public domain)
eu20-austria-hungary-okie-1928.gloss: Drawn facsimiles of Austrian and Hungarian inspection marks with periods; shows year-bearing marks 1807-1866 and office-letter rows 1866-1872 (Bozen, Hall, Klagenfurt, Eger).

eu20-austria-hungary-mkeh-1867-1937.title: MKEH / Budapest Capital Government Office, "Belfoeldoen keszult nemesfem targyak femjelei 1867-tol 1937-ig" (hallmarks of domestic precious-metal objects 1867-1937), PDF
eu20-austria-hungary-mkeh-1867-1937.gloss: The Hungarian hallmarking office's own table of the 1867-1937 marks: larger and smaller silver objects with fineness 950/900/800/750 and the office mark P.

eu20-austria-hungary-mkeh-1937-1966.title: MKEH, "Belfoeldoen keszult nemesfem targyak femjelei 1937-tol 1966-ig" (domestic hallmarks 1937-1966), PDF
eu20-austria-hungary-mkeh-1937-1966.gloss: Table of the 1937 marks: silver 935/900/800, larger objects with the Diana head, smaller with an animal head.

eu20-austria-hungary-mkeh-import-1867-19.title: MKEH, "Kulfoldrol behozott nemesfem targyak femjelei 1867-tol 1937-ig" (hallmarks of imported objects 1867-1937), PDF
eu20-austria-hungary-mkeh-import-1867-19.gloss: Import marks of 1867-68, 1868-72, 1872-1902 and 1902-1937, gold and silver.

eu20-austria-hungary-mkeh-history.title: MKEH, "A nemesfemvizsgalat tortenete" (history of precious-metal testing in Hungary)
eu20-austria-hungary-mkeh-history.gloss: Hallmarking compulsory from 1867 (Compromise), Royal Chief Hallmarking and Bullion Office in Budapest; the new hallmarking law took effect 1 September 1937 and changed fineness grades and mark designs.

eu20-austria-hungary-mkeh-rajzolatok.title: MKEH, "Femjelek rajzolatai" (index of valid Hungarian hallmarks 1867 to today)
eu20-austria-hungary-mkeh-rajzolatok.gloss: Index page: valid Hungarian hallmarks 1867-1937, 1937-1966, 1966-1999 and later, domestic and imported.

eu20-austria-hungary-mak-ws-1780-1866.title: MAK Vienna, Wiener Silber 1780-1866, vol. 2 (catalogue), entry 792: two sugar tongs, "oesterreichische Feingehaltspunze 1872-1922 (Dianakopf im Fuenfpass, Amtszeichen P = Pest)"
eu20-austria-hungary-mak-ws-1780-1866.gloss: Museum catalogue entry describing a Diana head in a five-lobed frame with the office letter P for Pest as the Austrian fineness stamp of 1872-1922. Seen only as a search-result snippet; the viewer page itself is behind a bot check and was not retrieved.

eu20-austria-hungary-bgbl-1954-212.title: Bundesgesetzblatt fuer die Republik Oesterreich 1954, 42. Stueck, Nr. 212 (3 Sept 1954): Verordnung des BM fuer Finanzen vom 24 Juni 1954 ueber den Feingehalt der Edelmetallgegenstaende (Durchfuehrungsverordnung zum Punzierungsgesetz, BGBl. 68/1954)
eu20-austria-hungary-bgbl-1954-212.gloss: Silver fineness 925/900/835/800; official stamps: hoopoe head with 1/2/3 for 925/900/835, toucan head with 4 for 800, dove wing with 1-4 for foreign goods; Punzierungsgesetz in force 1 July 1954; para. 74 recognises older stamps under the imperial ordinance of 26 May 1866 (RGBl. 75) and the law of 23 May 1875 (RGBl. 80). Copy of the RIS original, OCR text.

eu20-austria-hungary-cs-wiki-puncovnictv.title: Czech Wikipedia, "Puncovnictvi"
eu20-austria-hungary-cs-wiki-puncovnictv.gloss: Background only: medieval origins, current Czech marks under Act 539/1992; not used for specific marks.

eu20-austria-hungary-epravo-71-1949.title: Vyhlaska c. 71/1949 Sb. (Ministry of Industry, 25 Jan 1949): official marks for platinum, gold and silver goods
eu20-austria-hungary-epravo-71-1949.gloss: Cites the hallmarking act of 16 Dec 1927 No. 2 Sb. (1928); describes the Slovak-woman head marks for larger silver goods (grades 1-5) and the chamois head for smaller goods, the lily with C-caron for imports.

eu20-austria-hungary-wiki-silver-hallmar.title: English Wikipedia, "Silver hallmarks", section Hungary
eu20-austria-hungary-wiki-silver-hallmar.gloss: States the crowned-crescent Diana head with fineness-coded frame (five petals 800, hexagon 900) was used by Austria-Hungary and Hungary from 1867 to 1933 (the 1933 end date disagrees with the official Hungarian sources).

eu20-belgium-be-law-1868.title: Loi relative a la liberte du travail des matieres d'or et d'argent (20 juin 1868) and Arrete royal reglant le type des matrices et la forme des poincons de titre (1 juillet 1868), in Revue de la numismatique belge, 3e serie, t. I (1869), Actes officiels, pp. 86-92
eu20-belgium-be-law-1868.gloss: Official texts reprinted in 1869. Art. 1: manufacture free at all standards, compulsory State control abolished; Art. 2: silver may be submitted voluntarily for assay at 900 (1st) or 800 (2nd); Art. 6: in force 1 July 1869, repealing the law of 19 brumaire an VI and the arrete of 14 Sept 1814. The royal decree fixes the silver punches: Gothic capital A with 1 in a triangle with cut corners (1st standard) and Gothic A with 2 at upper right in a square with cut corners (2nd).

eu20-belgium-be-law-1987.title: Loi du 11 aout 1987 relative a la garantie des ouvrages en metaux precieux (consolidated text, refli.be)
eu20-belgium-be-law-1987.gloss: Art. 3: silver standards 925 (1st) and 835 (2nd) per mille; Art. 6: the title mark is 'AG' for silver followed by the figure; Art. 3, 10, 10bis: State punch and approved assay-body marks; Art. 13: maker's signature punch plus title punch.

eu20-belgium-nl-wiki-gehalteteken.title: Wikipedia (nl): Gehalteteken
eu20-belgium-nl-wiki-gehalteteken.gloss: States that silver marks since 1814 include a standing lion in a shield with 1 or I (first standard), a running lion in a lying hexagon with 2 or II (second), an old small sword, and after 1953 a sword with 925 or 835; also a stylised Z with I or II. Belgian section: tree branch / sword / leaf wreaths with 1 and 2 (1815-1832), harp with 1 or Janus head with 2 (1832-1869), Gothic A with 1 or 2 (1869-1942), flower with 1 or 2 (since 1942); 1987 law standards 925/835.

eu20-belgium-silvercollection-be.title: silvercollection.it: Belgium silver and gold hallmarks
eu20-belgium-silvercollection-be.gloss: Collector reference (G. Busetto). Captions: .934 and .833, warranty mark and office mark Gand (D) 1814-1831; .950 and .800 marks, warranty mark and office Liege (D) 1831-1868; .900 and .800 voluntary mark 1869-1942; 1942-1990 voluntary system with a four-petal flower and the letter A plus the fineness in an oval; AG with .925 / .835 after 1990.

eu20-belgium-stb-1951-215.title: Staatsblad 1951, no. 215: Wet van 15 Juni 1951 houdende goedkeuring en uitvoering van het Verdrag tot unificatie van accijnzen en van het waarborgrecht (Benelux, 18 Feb 1950)
eu20-belgium-stb-1951-215.gloss: The amending act: rewrites Art. 1 of the Waarborgwet to 925/835 for silver and, in the Benelux treaty annexed (ch. IV, Art. 20 par. 3), fixes the same silver standards (925, 835, and 800 on ministerial designation) for the Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg.

eu20-denmark-dk-bek-1457-2018.title: BEK nr 1457 af 10/12/2018 Bekendtgørelse om Ædelmetalkontrollens virksomhed (historisk), § 6 and annex 1
eu20-denmark-dk-bek-1457-2018.gloss: Executive order (now historical): the Assay Office's control stamp shows, in an oval frame, three towers and below them a wavy line followed by five horizontal lines; six sizes from 5.5 to 0.75 mm.

eu20-denmark-dk-bek-934-2020.title: BEK nr 934 af 23/06/2020 Bekendtgørelse om anmeldelse, registrering, stempling af og kontrol med varer af ædle metaller, § 9 and annex 3
eu20-denmark-dk-bek-934-2020.gloss: Current order under lov nr. 798 af 9 June 2020: goods need a name stamp (navnestempel) and a fineness stamp (holdighedsstempel); the Safety Authority's control stamp exists in two variants and six sizes; the Convention's common control stamp is recognised.

eu20-denmark-dk-lsf-122-2019.title: Forslag til lov om ædle metaller og konfliktmineraler (L 122, 2019-20), bemærkninger
eu20-denmark-dk-lsf-122-2019.gloss: Government bill text: the first Danish law on control of precious-metal articles came into force on 1 July 1961; goods made before 1 July 1961 are exempted from the new law.

eu20-denmark-dk-convention.title: Hallmarking Convention, country profile: Denmark
eu20-denmark-dk-convention.gloss: Contracting State since 1988; control marking voluntary; authorised assay office Ædelmetalkontrollen (FORCE Technology, Brøndby); CCM recognised; silver standards 999, 990, 958, 925, 835, 830, 800.

eu20-denmark-silvercollection-dk.title: Dictionary of hallmarks: Denmark (A Small Collection of Antique Silver)
eu20-denmark-silvercollection-dk.gloss: Private collector reference (not a dealer). Copenhagen's ancient three-towers mark became the national mark in 1893 and was abandoned in the early 1960s; a different version was adopted in 1988; assay masters (Hinnerup 1840-63, Groth 1863-1904, Heise 1904-32, Siggaard 1932-60, Hansen 1960-71, Hove 1971-74, Beyer 1974-88); fineness .826 earlier, .830 from about 1911, .800 minimum since 1988; numerals of .800 and above may be followed by S.

eu20-denmark-force-history.title: Lidt historie om Ædelmetalkontrollen (FORCE Technology PDF)
eu20-denmark-force-history.gloss: A short history from the Danish assay office. NOT opened directly (the URL returned 404 to the fetch tool); known only from a search-engine excerpt that says: three towers used in several towns and the capital before 1893, oldest example 1608; 1893 minimum 13 1/4 lødig (about 828) 'Prøvesølv' until 1972; four elements from 1893: maker's mark, fineness number, three towers, assay master's initials.

eu20-denmark-digitaltmuseum-skje.title: Rokokkoskje av sølv, 1793 (DigitaltMuseum, Nordenfjeldske Kunstindustrimuseum)
eu20-denmark-digitaltmuseum-skje.gloss: Catalogue entry: Copenhagen city mark described as three towers above the year number 93, with master mark, month mark and guardein F in a wreath.

eu20-finland-leimat-year.title: Year marks (Leimat.fi, Finnish hallmark guide run with the Tukes register)
eu20-finland-leimat-year.gloss: Full table: Finnish series began with A in 1810 (letter alone until 1833), letters J, W, Å, Ä, Ö never used, number after the letter changes after each 24 letters; A: 1810, 1834, 1858, 1882, 1906, 1930, 1954, 1978, 2002, 2026. Notes 1810 transition: three-crown control mark with D3 on a Porvoo spoon.

eu20-finland-leimat-control.title: Control marks (Leimat.fi)
eu20-finland-leimat-control.gloss: Alderman's zigzag 1689-1754; three crowns 1754-1809; one crown 1810-2021; oval import crown 1925-1998; angular export crown 1974-1998; CCM from 1975.

eu20-finland-leimat-regs.title: Regulations (Leimat.fi historical guide)
eu20-finland-leimat-regs.gloss: Timeline of Finnish hallmark law: 1752 act (effective 1754), 1759 year marks, 1810 Finnish assay office in Turku with a one-crown control mark, 1827 move to Helsinki, 1891/1893 fineness marks standardised (813 from 1892), 1925 compulsory marking and oval import crown, 1972 H dropped, 1975 Vienna Convention in force, 2000 Act, 2026 rules; silver standards over time.

eu20-finland-leimat-other.title: Unusual marks in a Finnish hallmark series (Leimat.fi)
eu20-finland-leimat-other.gloss: Worked examples: X5 = 1927, K6 = 1939 (with Turku locality mark A), oval import control mark from 1925, 813H marks, 13L beside 813 in 1892, rectangular outline with H from 1895, Norwegian 830S on imports.

eu20-finland-leimat-locality.title: Locality marks (Leimat.fi)
eu20-finland-leimat-locality.gloss: Lists 61 localities with marks; oldest from the 1600s; marks may be a coat of arms, name, abbreviation or single letter; a locality mark shows where the article was marked or inspected, not necessarily made.

eu20-finland-silvercollection-fi.title: Dictionary of hallmarks: Finland (A Small Collection of Antique Silver)
eu20-finland-silvercollection-fi.gloss: Private collector reference (not a dealer). National control mark: crown in a heart-shaped contour since 1810; import mark crown in an oval 1925-1998; new date-letter sequence from 1810; fineness mark table agreeing with Leimat; town marks symbols, names or initials, central supply from 1925, about 35 approved today; Convention member 1975.

eu20-finland-convention-fi.title: Hallmarking Convention, country profile: Finland
eu20-finland-convention-fi.gloss: Contracting State since 1975; Act 1029/2000 and Decree 1148/2000; supervisory authority Tukes; silver standards 999, 925, 830, 800; CCM recognised.

eu20-italy-it-dlgs-251-1999.title: Decreto legislativo 22 maggio 1999, n. 251: Disciplina dei titoli e dei marchi di identificazione dei metalli preziosi (Normattiva text)
eu20-italy-it-dlgs-251-1999.gloss: Art. 3: legal silver standards 925 and 800 per mille (any higher standard allowed); Art. 4: objects must carry the standard and the identification mark; Art. 28 repeals law 30 Jan 1968, n. 46; Art. 27 applies DPR 1496/1970 until the new regulation.

eu20-italy-it-dpr-150-2002.title: Decreto del Presidente della Repubblica 30 maggio 2002, n. 150: regolamento per l'applicazione del d.lgs. 251/1999
eu20-italy-it-dpr-150-2002.gloss: Art. 1(d): the identification mark is a polygonal impression containing a five-pointed star, the characteristic number assigned to the firm and the abbreviation of the province of its registered office; Art. 12: five sizes, engraved not in relief; Art. 16: the standard is struck in a normalised figure; repeals DPR 1496/1970.

eu20-italy-giancane-2020.title: Gianni Giancane, 'Particolari punzonature in area italiana. Individuazione e metodi di indagine', Antiqua nuova serie (10 April 2020)
eu20-italy-giancane-2020.gloss: Scholarly article. Law 2 May 1872 n. 806 set title punches 950/900/800 (800 often with Italia turrita and a 3), effective 1 June 1873; marking largely optional to 1934/35, often just a free-standing 800; law 5 Feb 1934 n. 305 and regulation 27 Dec 1934 n. 2393 (fascio lozenge, c. 1935-1944); D.Lgs.Lgt. 26 Oct 1944 n. 313 removed the fascio; law 30 Jan 1968 n. 46 led to new punches from 19 Sept 1971 (star in an elongated lozenge, elongated oval for the 800).

eu20-italy-silvercollection-it.title: silvercollection.it / ASCAS: Italian silver hallmarks (G. Busetto)
eu20-italy-silvercollection-it.gloss: Collector reference: 1872 optional official purity marks 950/900/800; unofficial '800'; 1934 lozenge with number, fascio and province letters plus an oval 800 or 925; 1944 lozenge without fascio; 1968/1970 polygonal mark with a star at left, number and province, ovals 925, 835, 800.

eu20-italy-camcom-na-storia.title: Camera di Commercio di Napoli, Ufficio metrico: 'Marchi nella storia'
eu20-italy-camcom-na-storia.gloss: Chamber of commerce page: law 806 of 2 May 1872 unified gold and silver titles and made the producer's mark optional; law 305 of 5 Feb 1934: silver title in an oval, gold in a hexagon, producer identified by a numeric code in a lozenge with province and fascio littorio, producer's mark mandatory; D.Lgs. 313 of 26 Oct 1944 removed the fascio; law 46 of 30 Jan 1968 gave the forms still in use; d.lgs. 251/99 left them unchanged.

eu20-italy-treccani-metalli.title: Enciclopedia Italiana (Treccani), 'Metalli' (appendix entry on the law on titles of precious metals)
eu20-italy-treccani-metalli.gloss: Law 5 Feb 1934 n. 305, 'Disciplina dei titoli dei metalli preziosi', and the regulation by royal decree 27 Dec 1934 n. 2393: producer's mark made of a code for each province and a progressive number per firm, followed by the title in thousandths.

eu20-italy-gu-1991-marchi.title: Gazzetta Ufficiale n. 4, 5 January 1991: Ministero dell'industria, Comunicato 'Provvedimenti concernenti i marchi di identificazione dei metalli preziosi'
eu20-italy-gu-1991-marchi.gloss: Official list of firms that ceased using their identification marks, each given as number plus province sigla (e.g. 359 AL Davide & Briata, Valenza).

eu20-netherlands-stb-1951-526.title: Staatsblad van het Koninkrijk der Nederlanden 1951, no. 526: Besluit van 29 November 1951 tot plaatsing van de tekst van de Waarborgwet 1927 (Stb. 48), zoals laatstelijk gewijzigd bij de Wet van 15 Juni 1951 (Stb. 215)
eu20-netherlands-stb-1951-526.gloss: Official consolidated text of the Dutch hallmarking act: Art. 1 sets silver at 925 and 835 thousandths (800 for objects designated by the Minister of Finance); Art. 10 lists the four state marks (fineness mark, office mark, year-letter mark, weight mark).

eu20-netherlands-stb-1951-215.title: Staatsblad 1951, no. 215: Wet van 15 Juni 1951 houdende goedkeuring en uitvoering van het Verdrag tot unificatie van accijnzen en van het waarborgrecht (Benelux, 18 Feb 1950)
eu20-netherlands-stb-1951-215.gloss: The amending act: rewrites Art. 1 of the Waarborgwet to 925/835 for silver and, in the Benelux treaty annexed (ch. IV, Art. 20 par. 3), fixes the same silver standards (925, 835, and 800 on ministerial designation) for the Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg.

eu20-netherlands-waarborg-plate-2023.title: Keurtekenplaat Waarborgwet 2019 (version April 2023), WaarborgHolland / Edelmetaal Waarborg Nederland / Rijksinspectie Digitale Infrastructuur
eu20-netherlands-waarborg-plate-2023.gloss: Official one-page chart of the Dutch hallmarks in force: silver 925 (1st standard), 835 (2nd), 800 (3rd) as lion marks with I, II, III on large new objects; small objects; used objects marked Z I / Z II / Z; office marks; year letters 2010-2034; the international Common Control Mark.

eu20-netherlands-waarborg-plate-2016.title: Keurtekenplaat Waarborgwet (version February 2016), WaarborgHolland / EWN / Agentschap Telecom (copy hosted at marclange.nl)
eu20-netherlands-waarborg-plate-2016.gloss: Earlier edition of the same official chart: shows Minerva-head office marks on silver and the same year-letter grid 2010-2034. It is a re-issue by the same bodies, so not independent of the 2023 chart as to the year letters.

eu20-netherlands-waarborg-keurtekens.title: WaarborgHolland, Keurtekens
eu20-netherlands-waarborg-keurtekens.gloss: Current page: silver standards 835 and 925; office marks and year letters apply to large objects; the Common Control Mark (Vienna Convention, in force internationally since 1975) is accepted.

eu20-netherlands-nl-wiki-gehalteteken.title: Wikipedia (nl): Gehalteteken
eu20-netherlands-nl-wiki-gehalteteken.gloss: States that silver marks since 1814 include a standing lion in a shield with 1 or I (first standard), a running lion in a lying hexagon with 2 or II (second), an old small sword, and after 1953 a sword with 925 or 835; also a stylised Z with I or II. Belgian section: tree branch / sword / leaf wreaths with 1 and 2 (1815-1832), harp with 1 or Janus head with 2 (1832-1869), Gothic A with 1 or 2 (1869-1942), flower with 1 or 2 (since 1942); 1987 law standards 925/835.

eu20-netherlands-nl-wiki-zilver.title: Wikipedia (nl): Zilver
eu20-netherlands-nl-wiki-zilver.gloss: Mentions the Dutch hallmark (gehalteteken, maker's mark, year-letter mark) granted by a state-designated assay body and the current standards 925, 835 (second) and 800 (third).

eu20-netherlands-bd-museum.title: Belasting & Douane Museum, collectie: Zilverwerk
eu20-netherlands-bd-museum.gloss: Museum of the Dutch tax and customs service, which holds the Waarborg collection: the Waarborg's assayers (essayeurs) tested and tax-marked silver from 1814; the tax on precious metal, introduced in the early 19th century, was abolished in 1953.

eu20-netherlands-silvercollection-nl.title: silvercollection.it (G. Busetto, ASCAS): Netherlands silver hallmarks since 1814
eu20-netherlands-silvercollection-nl.gloss: Private collector's reference. Says the Kingdom of the Netherlands adopted a standard national system in 1814, kept to 1953; .934 and .833 marks for large work, .833 for small; office marks in two versions (1814-1905 and from 1906) with identification letters; duty and restitution marks; date-letter table given as an image only.

eu20-netherlands-zilver-nl.title: zilver.nl, Zilvermerken (publisher: Old Memories B.V., a commercial site)
eu20-netherlands-zilver-nl.gloss: Says: since 1814 hallmarking has been national; small silver carries a sword shape plus the maker's mark; large silver carries four marks (maker's mark, Minerva head of the assay office, lion for the standard, year letter). Commercial publisher, used only for the general structure.

eu20-norway-snl-gullstempel.title: gullstempel og sølvstempel (Store norske leksikon)
eu20-norway-snl-gullstempel.gloss: Norway's national encyclopedia: oldest order to stamp gold and silver 1314; 1491 town mark (crowned initial: crowned O Oslo, crowned B Bergen); 1891 minimum fineness 585 gold and 830 silver; usual stamps 925 S for jewellery, 830 S for cutlery and hollowware; maker marks registered with Patentstyret; 19th-century sets add fineness 13 1/2 L, year and month marks; guardein mark (initial plus W).

eu20-norway-silvercollection-no.title: Dictionary of hallmarks: Norway (A Small Collection of Antique Silver)
eu20-norway-silvercollection-no.gloss: Private collector reference (not a dealer). The modern Norwegian system came into effect after the 1891 Act; in 1892 silver fineness was standardised at .830 and 830S became compulsory; from 1920 .925 began to replace .830; 1931 and 1947 quality marks; member of the Hallmarking Convention since 1983.

eu20-norway-convention-no.title: Hallmarking Convention, country profile: Norway
eu20-norway-convention-no.gloss: Contracting State since 1983; voluntary control system; Law 2010-09-03, Regulation 2011-01-10; authorised assay office Justervesenet (Kjeller); silver standards 999, 925, 830, 800; CCM recognised.

eu20-norway-digitaltmuseum-skje.title: Rokokkoskje av sølv (DigitaltMuseum, Nordenfjeldske Kunstindustrimuseum)
eu20-norway-digitaltmuseum-skje.gloss: Catalogue entry for a silver spoon of 1793 with Copenhagen city mark, master and guardein marks and a month mark; shows how Norwegian-Danish sets carried town, master, guardein, year/month marks (cited for the pre-1891 system only).

eu20-sweden-sfs-1999-780.title: Förordning (1999:780) om handel med ädelmetallarbeten, 15-18 §§ (Ordinance on trade in precious-metal articles)
eu20-sweden-sfs-1999-780.gloss: Current ordinance. §16: the year mark is one of 24 letters A-Z without J and W (A B C D E F G H I K L M N O P Q R S T U V X Y Z), used in sequence one per year, A = 1759, followed by a number for the round of the letter series. §15: town marks show place of manufacture or importer's home town, fixed by Swedac. §18: the control stamp is three crowns in a trefoil-shaped shield followed by S for silver (P for platinum).

eu20-sweden-sv-wp-kontrollstampel.title: Kontrollstämpel (Swedish Wikipedia)
eu20-sweden-sv-wp-kontrollstampel.gloss: Royal ordinance of 7 Dec 1752, in force 1 Jan 1754: the state's three crowns in a trefoil ('kattfoten') replaced the alderman's zigzag. 1759: uniform year letters, A = 1759, no J, W, Å, Ä, Ö. 1860: town marks simplified to letters. Stockholm used the city crown, then from 1689 St Eric. 1912 act: oval three-crowns stamp for imported gold and silver, in force 1 Jan 1913; 1912 also set silver at 830/1000. 1974 law: carat marks replaced by per mille, 830 as silver floor, 925 for sterling; since 1975 the Convention's balance-scale mark may replace the kattfot; Lag 1986:985 made control stamping voluntary.

eu20-sweden-runeberg-1914.title: Sweden: Historical and Statistical Handbook, 2nd part, 'Hall-marking of Gold, Silver and Pewter Wares' (K. A. Wallroth), 1914
eu20-sweden-runeberg-1914.gloss: Contemporary account: Hall Marks Act of 7 Dec 1752, Assay Office 1753, Mint and Assay Office 1910, new Act of 1912. Silver 830/1000 minimum, one quality only, no standard mark. Required stamps: maker, place, date mark from 1759. Silver hallmark: three crowns in a heart-shaped (trefoil) shield followed by an S; foreign wares in an oval shield.

eu20-sweden-sou-2026-14.title: SOU 2026:14, Ädelmetallutredningen: En moderniserad reglering av handel med ädelmetallarbeten
eu20-sweden-sou-2026-14.gloss: Official 2026 government inquiry. The kattfot (small coat of arms, three crowns in a trefoil shield) has been used since 1754; two variants existed (trefoil for Swedish-made, oval for imported), both in the 1974 law; the oval was dropped in the 1986 law. Control stamping has been voluntary since the 1986 law; year marks and town marks are voluntary responsibility stamps.

eu20-sweden-hallmarking-convention-se.title: Hallmarking Convention, country profile: Sweden
eu20-sweden-hallmarking-convention-se.gloss: Sweden a Contracting State since 1975; legal basis includes Förordning 1975:49 on the common control mark; Swedac supervises, RISE (Borås) is the authorised assay office; CCM recognised; silver standards 999, 990, 958, 925, 835, 830, 800.

eu20-sweden-silvercollection-se.title: Dictionary of hallmarks: Sweden (A Small Collection of Antique Silver)
eu20-sweden-silvercollection-se.gloss: Private collector reference (not a dealer). Dates the present form of the national control mark (three crowns in a trefoil on a striated ground) to 1901; S in a hexagonal frame for .800; oval import mark 1912-1988; town marks standardised after 1912 (about 140), usually the town's initial in a square or circle, only Stockholm a crowned figure; year and town marks optional from 1988. Cites W5 struck for V5 (1875).

eu20-sweden-commons-c10.title: File:C10 silver hallmark.jpg (Wikimedia Commons)
eu20-sweden-commons-c10.gloss: Spoon marked C10, described as made 1977 (C10 = 1977 on the A=1759 24-letter rule).

eu20-sweden-commons-svensknyare.title: File:Svensknyare.JPG (Wikimedia Commons)
eu20-sweden-commons-svensknyare.gloss: Swedish silver marks 'svenska silverstämplar 1956' (spoon with F9, which is 1956 on the rule).

eu20-sweden-commons-visby.title: File:Hallmarks for Sophies Silver in Visby, Sweden.jpg (Wikimedia Commons)
eu20-sweden-commons-visby.gloss: Ring marked W (Visby), 925, D11 (stated as 2002), ASQ (maker).

eu20-sweden-commons-kattfot.title: File:Kattfot guldstämpel (Kontrollstämpel).png (Wikimedia Commons)
eu20-sweden-commons-kattfot.gloss: Image of the kattfot, the Swedish hallmark of purity and authenticity, three crowns in a trefoil.

eu20-switzerland-bazg-1880.title: Swiss Federal Customs (BAZG/EZV), Central Office for Precious Metals Control: "Reproduction of the ancient official hallmarks since 1880" (German: "Abbildungen der ehemaligen amtlichen Stempel seit 1880"), 2-page PDF
eu20-switzerland-bazg-1880.gloss: Drawings with fineness for the marks of the Precious Metals Control Act of 23.12.1880 (watch cases: Helvetia 750, squirrel 583, bear 875, capercaillie 800, chamois head platinum 950 from 10.02.1914), the 1917 import marks (lynx, edelweiss, E, A), and the Act of 20.06.1933 (Helvetia 750, squirrel 585, morning star 375, duck 925, capercaillie 800, ibex 950; imported watch cases lynx 1/2, TB, gentian 1/2, hare head).

eu20-switzerland-bazg-stamping.title: BAZG, "Edelmetallkontrolle - Pruefung und Stempelung von Uhrgehaeusen"
eu20-switzerland-bazg-stamping.gloss: States that the St Bernard head ("Bernhardinerkopf") is the official stamp for all precious metals and all finenesses, carrying the mark of the testing office at the cross; official stamps since 1880 listed in a linked PDF.

eu20-switzerland-bazg-convention.title: BAZG, "Edelmetallkontrolle - Internationale Uebereinkommen, Rechtsgrundlagen"
eu20-switzerland-bazg-convention.gloss: Vienna Convention of 1972 and the common control mark (a scales symbol); table of fineness values for silver 800, 925, 999 (also gold, platinum, palladium).

eu20-switzerland-hls-edelmetalle.title: Anne-Marie Dubler, "Edelmetalle", Historisches Lexikon der Schweiz (HLS) (2004), section Edelmetallkontrolle
eu20-switzerland-hls-edelmetalle.gloss: Federal law of 1880 (revised 1933, partly revised 1995) took over control from the cantons, central office in Bern; Switzerland joined the Vienna Convention in 1975; watch cases carry the official punch (St Bernard head since 1995); jewellery carries fineness and responsibility mark. CC BY-SA.

eu20-switzerland-emkv-1934.title: Edelmetallkontrollverordnung (EMKV), SR 941.311, Federal Council ordinance of 8 May 1934 (as of 2 Aug 2013), implementing the Act of 20 June 1933 (SR 941.31)
eu20-switzerland-emkv-1934.gloss: Art. 109: appearance and size of the official stamps are set by Annex no. 1; Schlussbestimmung of 19 June 1995: goods with the new rules but still an old official stamp may stay on the market; repeals the Federal Council decisions of 1916-1932, incl. the 16 June 1917 decision on imported gold, silver and platinum goods.

eu20-switzerland-wiki-silberstempel.title: German Wikipedia, "Silberstempel", section Schweiz
eu20-switzerland-wiki-silberstempel.gloss: Control stamps: bear for 875, capercaillie (Auerhahn) for 800, each with a letter for the canton; system standardised 1887 and changed 1893 (cantonal marking after the 1848 constitution).

eu20-switzerland-commons-ch.title: Wikimedia Commons file page: Reproduction of the ancient Swiss official hallmarks since 1880.png (licence CC0, author Swiss Federal Precious Metals Control)
eu20-switzerland-commons-ch.gloss: Licence declaration for the BAZG reproduction (CC0 1.0). The file Barry large.jpg (St Bernard head) carries the same CC0 declaration (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Barry_large.jpg).

nl-yl-zk-kaart.title: Zilver.nl Keurendatabase: Jaarletterkaart, plate 5.18 'De jaarletters van 1814-2009 / The date letters of 1814-2009' (scanned page image of a printed reference book; image keuren.zilver.nl/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/jaaletters.jpg)
nl-yl-zk-kaart.gloss: Image with all 196 years 1814-2009, each stamp drawn with its year, footnotes (1)-(7) cut off at the edge. Covers every row. Run by zilver.nl, a commercial antiques shop (allowed as a reference table; the book it reproduces is not named on the page). Its text also says: first alphabet began with E in 1814 as continuation of a,b,c,d of the Kingdom of Holland; J of the 6th alphabet stayed in use until 1 June 1945, then a small k was used 1 June 1945 to end 1946; N of the 6th alphabet crowned from July 1948 (Juliana); V of the 7th alphabet crowned from 1 May 1980 (Beatrix). zilver.nl/content/jaarletters.html is the same publisher (counted as the same source). Separately published table; it does not name its own source, so it may share an ancestor with the other tables (Dutch Wikipedia cites Luijt, Het Zilverlexicon, 2006).

nl-yl-zz-1814-2034.title: Zaanse Zilversmeden: 'Jaarletters van 1814 - 2034' (table image on 'Zilvermerken herkennen')
nl-yl-zz-1814-2034.gloss: Image (wp-content/uploads/2026/07/jaarletters-1814-2034-2-1.png) of drawn stamps with year captions 1814-2034, one panel per 25-year cycle. A Zaan-region silversmith history site, non-commercial as far as seen. Layout differs from zk-kaart (stamps are re-drawn), so treated as a separate table, but it may share an ancestor (see problems). Separately published table; it does not name its own source, so it may share an ancestor with the other tables (Dutch Wikipedia cites Luijt, Het Zilverlexicon, 2006).

nl-yl-sc-1814-1953.title: A Small Collection of Antique Silver (ASCAS), Netherlands old marks: 'Kingdom of the Netherlands: date letters 1814-1953' (image WORLDOLANDA101.10BIS.jpg)
nl-yl-sc-1814-1953.gloss: Image table 1814-1953 (letters not in page text; image fetched with a browser User-Agent and Referer because the site answers curl with 999). Reads 1870 as a hatched blank stamp (illegible). Separately published table; it does not name its own source, so it may share an ancestor with the other tables (Dutch Wikipedia cites Luijt, Het Zilverlexicon, 2006).

nl-yl-sc-after-1953.title: A Small Collection of Antique Silver (ASCAS), Netherlands: 'Date letters after 1953' (image NETHERLANDMARK7bis.jpg)
nl-yl-sc-after-1953.gloss: Typeset table 1953-2019, same site as sc-1814-1953 but a different image and layout; counted as the same publisher for independence but listed separately because it covers other years. Agrees with zk-kaart except 1979-1985, where it runs one letter ahead and lists two stamps for 1985 (z and A): see disagreements. Separately published table; it does not name its own source, so it may share an ancestor with the other tables (Dutch Wikipedia cites Luijt, Het Zilverlexicon, 2006).

nl-yl-nl-wiki-jaarletter.title: Wikipedia (nl): Jaarletter, with five Commons image tables 'Jaarletters 1810-1834 ... 1910-1934 Nederland' (CC BY-SA)
nl-yl-nl-wiki-jaarletter.gloss: Image tables for 1810-1934 (1810-1813 a,b,c,d script of the Kingdom of Holland; 1814 E ...). Text gives cycle character per series, notes strokes above some letters, says 1956 should have had V but got W, and cites Luijt, Het Zilverlexicon voor Nederland en Belgie (2006). The text claims J is skipped in every cycle, which its own 1910-1934 table contradicts (J 1919). Separately published table; it does not name its own source, so it may share an ancestor with the other tables (Dutch Wikipedia cites Luijt, Het Zilverlexicon, 2006).

nl-yl-delpher-1949-de-jaarletters.title: Newspaper article 'De jaarletters' (and 'Zilver kopen: leer de keuren kennen!'), 6 Jan 1949; same text syndicated in Breda, Enschede, Rotterdam papers 8 Jan, 13 Jan, 1 Apr 1949
nl-yl-delpher-1949-de-jaarletters.gloss: Gives the alphabets by period and style, and 1940=F, 1945=K with crown, 1946=L plain, 1948=N crowned. The syndicated copies are one source.

nl-yl-delpher-1934-keurteekens.title: Newspaper 1934 'Keurteekens op zilver' (urn ddd:010663133:mpeg21:a0319)
nl-yl-delpher-1934-keurteekens.gloss: Nineteenth alphabet began with A in 1910; in 1934 the year letter Z is struck.

nl-yl-delpher-1971-goud.title: Newspaper 1971 article on gold marks (urn ddd:010957610:mpeg21:a0252)
nl-yl-delpher-1971-goud.gloss: 'De jaarletter van het goud. R is 1953.' Gold, but struck with the same national letter.

nl-yl-delpher-1980-waarborg-advertentie.title: Waarborg advertisement 'Jaarletter in zilverwerk', Stadsarchief Vlaardingen 20 Aug 1980 (also NRC 26 Apr 1980 ad, urn ddd:011200784:mpeg21:a1187, and Gerritsen ad 1 May 1980)
nl-yl-delpher-1980-waarborg-advertentie.gloss: States that, as in 1948, a special year letter was fixed for 1980: a 'v' in small script letters with a royal crown, in a circle, valid to 31 Dec 1980.

nl-yl-rijks-bulletin-1978-jaffe.title: A. L. den Blaauwen, 'Schenking Jaffe-Pierson', The Rijksmuseum Bulletin 26(3), 1978, pp. 113-126 (doi 10.52476/trb.20920)
nl-yl-rijks-bulletin-1978-jaffe.gloss: Catalogue of 50 Amsterdam silver pieces, each giving the keurkamer head (a = Amsterdam) and 'jaarletter x (year)'. Cataloguer writes letters in lower case throughout, so case is not evidence.

nl-yl-rijks-collection-data.title: Rijksmuseum collection catalogue records (CC0), description search 'jaarletter'

nl-yl-zilver-nl-jaarletters.title: zilver.nl Kennisbank: Jaarletters (same publisher as zk-kaart)
nl-yl-zilver-nl-jaarletters.gloss: Commercial antiques shop (allowed as reference). Text: began 1814 with E to Z; example year letter O = 1873 on Amsterdam silver. Counted with zk-kaart as one source. Separately published table; it does not name its own source, so it may share an ancestor with the other tables (Dutch Wikipedia cites Luijt, Het Zilverlexicon, 2006).

nl-yl-stcrt-2008-1070.title: Staatscourant 2008 nr. 232 p. 1070 (and Stcrt 2009 nr. 19164): Waarborgregeling Annex IV 'Jaarlettermerken'
nl-yl-stcrt-2008-1070.gloss: States that Annex IV of the Waarborgregeling lists the year-letter marks up to and including 2009 and that new ones were fixed for 2010-2034. Confirms 2009 as the end of the older series but does not print the letters (annex of the pre-2010 regulation was only held at the Waarborg offices, Stcrt 1997 nr 249).

nl-yl-nl-wiki-hallmark-law.title: Dutch Waarborgwet 1927 as consolidated 1951 (Stb 1951, 526), art. 10: the state marks include a year-letter mark
nl-yl-nl-wiki-hallmark-law.gloss: Context only; does not give letters.

entries.name: Prague office B with 15 and year, 1807-1824
entries.looks_like: A shield with a bell-shaped top holding the letter B; below it an oval cut into four by a cross holding the numeral 15, with the four digits of a year around the oval (1 8 0 7 on this example).
entries.means: Silver of 15 lot (937.5/1000), assayed at the Prague office (B), the year in the mark (example 1807). Lot system, before the 1824 law.
entries.eu20_note: The Czech office says these year-bearing forms were used 1807-1824; Okie dates the Prague 1814 form "1814-1866". The 1824 law then fixed the 1824-1866 year marks.

sources.where: page 7, marks 1807-1824 and the office letters A-L
printed p. 357, Prague row, B marks 1807-1813

entries.means: Silver of 13 lot (812.5/1000) under the law of 1 April 1824, with that year's date in the mark; valid for all Austria except Cracow, Hungary, Lombardy and Venetia. Example shown 1866.
entries.eu20_note: A new year number was struck each year; marks of Vienna carried A in place of B (Okie p. 359), other offices their own letters.

entries.name: Diana head with 1 in a cloud-like frame (950/1000), 1867-1922
entries.looks_like: The head of Diana in profile facing right, a crescent moon at the forehead, in a cloud-like frame with six rounded lobes; the numeral 1 beside the head and a small star where the office letter is struck.
entries.means: Larger silver object of 950/1000 fineness, Austria-Hungary. The numeral gives the fineness (1 = 950, 2 = 900, 3 = 800, 4 = 750) and the frame shape repeats it. The star marks the place of the assay-office letter (A Vienna, B Linz, C Prague ...) from 1872.
entries.eu20_note: Start date: Neuwirth 1867; the Czech office gives the law as 26 May 1866 in force 1 Aug 1866 and the VR stock mark from 26 May 1866; Wikipedia gives 1867 for Hungary. End: 22 April 1922 for Austria (Czech office), 28 Feb 1921 in the Czech lands, 1936/37 in Hungary. From 1867 to March 1872 the office letter was a separate punch (no star in the frame); the drawn image is the 1872 form with the star.

sources.where: pp. 86-87, Beilage B I and captions (fineness 1-4)
page 8, S-28 to S-31 and note that the stamps of RGBl. 75/1866 stayed in Austria to 1922

entries.means: Larger silver object of 800/1000, Hungary, new marks of the law of 1 September 1937 (silver grades 935, 900, 800).
entries.eu20_note: End 1966 per MKEH index (the 1937-1966 table); some collector forums say 1965. The Czech office text puts the end of the old Austrian stamps in Hungary at 1936.

entries.name: Second Czechoslovak mark, silver 1 (959/1000), 1929-1940
entries.looks_like: A triangle showing hills with a double-armed (Lorraine) cross on the top and the numeral 1 outlined across the slope.
entries.means: Silver of 959/1000 (grade 1 of five), Czechoslovakia, under the hallmarking act of 16 Dec 1927 (No. 2/1928 Sb.), in force 1 Jan 1929; decree 216/1928 Sb. Made in two sizes (larger and smaller goods). The 925 grade first appears here.
entries.eu20_note: Decree 216/1928 Sb. itself could not be fetched (aspi.cz unreachable); the grade-to-numeral order follows the Czech office table.

sources.where: page 9, S-44 to S-48 and the paragraph on act 2/1928 Sb. and decree 216/1928 Sb.
preamble: act of 16 Dec 1927, No. 2 Sb. (1928); marks stay in force into 1949

entries.name: Official title punches 950 / 900 / 800 (Italia turrita), from 1873
entries.looks_like: A small punch with the turreted head of Italia and the figure of the title (the 800 is described as with a 3); optional State punch for the first (950), second (900) and third (800) title.
entries.means: Optional State-controlled silver standards 950, 900 and 800 per mille, Kingdom of Italy.
entries.eu20_note: Rarely struck. The images on the collector page are described only by file name (a turreted head), so the exact shape is not described here. The collector and Giancane give the start as 1872/1873 (law of 2 May 1872, effective 1 June 1873).

sources.where: law 806/1872: punches 950, 900, 800; 800 often with Italia turrita and a 3; effective 1 June 1873
law 806 of 2 May 1872 unified the titles and made the mark optional

entries.name: Maker's lozenge with number, fasces and province (fascio mark), 1934/35-1944
entries.looks_like: A lozenge (truncated at the acute corners) holding a number, the fascio littorio and the two-letter province code; struck beside an oval with the title.
entries.means: The maker's registration number and province: the number is the firm's, the letters are the province of its registered office. Mandatory under law 305 of 5 Feb 1934.
entries.eu20_note: Start date: 1934 (the law) vs 1935 (Giancane gives 25 April 1935 as the date the framework took hold; the regulation was published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale of March 1935).

entries.name: How the star mark works: number plus province (system, with examples)
entries.looks_like: Star, a number and two letters: for example 359 AL.
entries.means: The number is a serial the chamber of commerce of the province assigns to a firm; the letters are the province's car-plate sigla (AL Alessandria, AR Arezzo, BG Bergamo); the same number can exist in different provinces. It identifies the maker or importer, not a year. The register of holders is kept by each chamber of commerce.
entries.eu20_note: Examples are firms that stopped using their marks, listed in the official gazette of 1991. The 1934-1944 lozenge used the same number-plus-province logic (example per Giancane: number 48 MI, Arno Fassi, Milan). Not every registration is listed here.

sources.where: Art. 1(d) and the register kept by the chambers of commerce
examples: 359 AL Davide & Briata (Valenza); 654 AR '2 S S.r.l.' (Arezzo); 10 BG Rongoni Armando (Calolziocorte)

entries.name: Assay-office mark: Minerva head with a letter, 1814-
entries.looks_like: A helmeted head of Minerva in a small frame; a letter in the helmet identifies the assay office; on large silver only, with the lion, year letter and maker's mark.
entries.means: Assay office (kantoor van waarborg) that tested the object, the Netherlands, 1814-1953 and in later forms.
entries.eu20_note: The statute names the office mark but not its picture; the Minerva head comes from zilver.nl and the 2016 official chart. The chart of 2023 (Waarborgwet 2019) shows different office marks (lion-head 'Nationaal' marks and an NL ASSAY OFFICE convention mark). The letter-to-office list (A Amsterdam, E Groningen, I Breda, J Joure) rests on one collector source and is not entered. One database claims the Minerva head only appeared in 1953; that conflicts with the rest and is not followed.

entries.name: 830 S, silver, 1891/1892 to today
entries.looks_like: The figures 830 followed by S ('sølv'), struck under the base or on a hidden part.
entries.means: Silver of at least 830/1000, the standard for cutlery and hollowware. The 1891 law set the minimum at 830 for silver; one source says 830S became compulsory in 1892.
entries.eu20_note: Start year: SNL says 1891; silvercollection-no says 1891 Act and 830S compulsory in 1892. The name of the 1891 act is not given in either source.

sources.where: 1891 minimum fineness 830; stamped '830 S' on cutlery and korpus

entries.looks_like: The figures 925 followed by S.
entries.means: Sterling silver (925/1000), the usual stamp for jewellery; replaced 830 as the main standard from about 1920.
entries.eu20_note: Start year from silvercollection-no only.

entries.name: Three crowns in a trefoil ('kattfoten'), national control mark, 1754 to today
entries.looks_like: Three crowns (the small Swedish coat of arms, two above one) inside a rounded trefoil shield, with a striated (cat's-paw) background.
entries.means: The Swedish state's guarantee that the piece was tested to the legal fineness. In use since 1754 on Swedish-made gold and silver; on silver it is followed by an S. Optional since the 1986 law.
entries.eu20_note: silvercollection-se dates the present form of the mark to 1901 (single source; not otherwise confirmed). The brief's '1912 three-crowns-in-trefoil mark' is the 1912 act, which kept the trefoil for Swedish work and added the oval for imports; the trefoil itself dates from 1754.

sources.where: Sverige section: royal ordinance 7 Dec 1752, in force 1 Jan 1754
section on the kattfot: used since 1754
Hallmark designs: three crowns in a heart-shaped shield

visual.holder: 24guld.se (uploader)
visual.credit: Image: 24guld.se, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons; converted to JPEG by Heirloom.

entries.name: S after the three crowns, silver, 1912 to today
entries.looks_like: A capital S in a small frame struck beside the three crowns; on the 1956 spoon examined it is an ornate S in a small round frame, and one collector reference describes a hexagonal frame.
entries.means: Silver (the three-crowns control mark followed by S). Under the 1912 act silver had one legal quality, 830/1000, with no number stamped; numerals 830 and 925 were added after the 1974 law.
entries.eu20_note: The S is described by Runeberg (1914) as already in use in 1914; the exact year it was introduced is not given by any of the sources found. silvercollection-se gives a hexagonal frame and a .800 meaning, which does not match the 830 minimum of the 1912 act; treated as unconfirmed.

sources.where: Hallmark designs: 'Silver: a similar hallmark, followed by an S'
18 §: three crowns followed by S for silver
Nyare bestämmelser: numbers stamped after the S

visual.holder: Wikimedia Commons
visual.credit: Photo: FBQ, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons; cropped by Heirloom.

entries.name: Three crowns in an oval, imported silver and gold, 1913 to 1986
entries.looks_like: The three crowns inside an oval shield instead of the trefoil.
entries.means: Foreign (imported) gold or silver tested and stamped in Sweden. Introduced by the 1912 act (in force 1 Jan 1913); no longer used after the 1986 law.
entries.eu20_note: End date: sv-wp says no longer obligatory from 4 Dec 1986 (Lag 1986:985); SOU 2026:14 says the oval was removed with the 1986 law but also that both variants were in the 1974 law; silvercollection-se says used until 1988. Taken as 1986.

sources.where: section 'Kontrollstämpel i oval sköld för importerade ädelmetallarbeten'

searched: Wikimedia Commons: 'Swedish hallmark', 'silverstämplar', 'kontrollstämpel silver', Category:Hallmarks of Sweden (no oval import mark photo)

entries.name: Year letter and series number, 1759 to today (A8 = 1927)
entries.looks_like: A capital letter followed by a small number, in a rectangular frame, e.g. C10.
entries.means: Year of marking. One letter per year in the 24-letter run A-Z without J, W, Å, Ä, Ö, A = 1759; the number counts the round. A7 = 1903, A8 = 1927, A9 = 1951, A10 = 1975, A11 = 1999, A12 = 2023. Voluntary since 1986/1988 but still used.
entries.eu20_note: The brief gave 'A8 = 1904'; by the law and three dated examples A8 is 1927 (A7 = 1903). So the 1904-1926 marks are B7 to Z7.

visual.credit: Photo: Wolfgangus Mozart, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons; saved as JPEG by Heirloom.

entries.name: Town marks (ortsmärken) as a system, 1860 to today
entries.looks_like: Usually the town's initial letter in a square or round frame; Stockholm differs (a crowned figure).
entries.means: Place where the piece was made or marked. Simplified to letters in 1860, standardised after 1912 (about 140 marks); optional since 1988; today fixed by Swedac for Swedish makers and importers.
entries.eu20_note: The ~140 figure is from one source only (silvercollection-se).

entries.means: Stockholm. The city crown was the first Stockholm town mark; from 1689 the figure of St Eric, still used.

entries.name: Göteborg: crowned G
entries.looks_like: A G under a crown.
entries.means: Göteborg; crowned G (earlier GB) used since at least the 1630s.
entries.eu20_note: silvercollection-se says only Stockholm uses a crowned figure after 1912; whether the 20th-century Göteborg mark still carries the crown is not confirmed.

entries.name: Fineness numerals 830 and 925 in a rectangle, 1974 to today
entries.looks_like: Three digits (830, 925, 800, ...) in a rectangular frame.
entries.means: Silver fineness in thousandths: 830 (the legal floor since 1912) and 925 (sterling). Before the 1974 law the fineness was not stamped (or was stamped after the S).
entries.eu20_note: The 'after the S' wording in sv-wp conflicts mildly with Runeberg (no standard mark for silver in 1914).

searched: Wikimedia Commons Swedish hallmark searches

entries.eu20_note: Convention marks are already Heirloom-wide; no Swedish image sought.

entries.name: Swiss bear, silver 875/1000, 1880-1933
entries.looks_like: A bear standing on its hind legs, walking left, in a tall shield with a notched side and a small cross (the place for the control-office mark).
entries.means: Official Swiss stamp for silver of 875/1000 on watch cases under the Precious Metals Control Act of 23 Dec 1880.
entries.eu20_note: The 1933 Act no longer lists the bear. Wikipedia says the stamp carries a canton letter; BAZG shows a cross where the office mark goes.

entries.looks_like: The head of a St Bernard dog in profile facing left, with a collar, in an irregular hexagonal frame with a small cross at the cheek.
entries.means: Today's Swiss official stamp ("amtlicher Stempel"): used for all precious metals and all finenesses, carrying the mark of the testing office at the cross; compulsory on watch cases, voluntary on other goods.
entries.eu20_note: The image was taken from the BAZG page original (156x122 px), which is the file Commons republished as Barry large.jpg.

sources.where: "Fuer alle Edelmetalle und alle Feingehalte wird der Bernhardinerkopf als amtlicher Stempel verwendet"

entries.name: Common control mark (Vienna Convention), scales
entries.looks_like: A balance scale in an octagon, struck beside a fineness number (for silver in a notched-rectangle frame: 800, 925, 999).
entries.means: The Vienna Convention common control mark; goods with it and an official stamp of a member state are not re-tested by other members. Silver finenesses 800, 925, 999. Switzerland joined in 1975 (HLS; the Convention itself dates from 1972).
entries.eu20_note: The Swiss responsibility mark (registered initials in circles) is described on the same pages but its image was left out for the same licence reason.
